Output 1: Strengthened inclusion and transparency of the electoral process. 1.1: 15.6% increase in voter registration especially women, youth and PWD. There are 18,103,603 voters (9,501,809 female, 8,601,794 male), and 65% youth. 1.2: 1.6% decline in the number of female candidates in all direct elective positions. It reduced from 6.5% in 2016 to 4.9% in 2021.
Output 2: Enhanced institutional capacity for EC and other electoral stakeholders. 2.1: 5% Increase in public trust in the EC. This increased from 42% in 2016 to 47% in 2021. 2.2: 3 institutions (the Electoral Commission, Uganda Human Rights Commission, and the Media Center of Uganda) have capacity to effectively support electoral processes in Uganda. 2.3: 1. A) No (0) operational ToT training (national) for EC was conducted B) No (0) operational ToT at (subnational) for EC was conducted C) One BRIDGE modular training was conducted and 3 SEPU staff participated in the 5 day virtual training. The BRIDGE training for the Electoral Commission was not conducted. 2. None (0) Training of Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs in electoral law/regulation drafting was conducted. 3) None (0) Operational trainings of Police, Judiciary & Media was conducted
Output 3: Strengthened dialogue capacities and electoral violence early warning and rapid response system (EWER) 3.1: There is an EWER systems at national and district level in place. It covers Central, Eastern, Western and Northern regions of Uganda. 3.2: 2 EWER systems partially include gender-data. The Early Warning and Early Response system is gender responsive and includes gender data. 3.3: 5 dialogue meetings were conducted in Central, Eastern, Northern, Western and Southern on mediation and consensus building.
Output 4: Effective and efficient management, partnership formation and monitoring and evaluation of the project 4.1: 8 Project staff were recruited on schedule. 4.2: 4 Partnerships in place with key national actors like the Electoral Commission (EC), Judiciary, Media Council of Uganda (MCU), Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC), Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, The Elders Forum of Uganda (TEFU) and Inter Religious Council of Uganda (IRCU) to support the electoral process. 4.3: 1 Project Mid-term Evaluation was not undertaken. It will be conducted in 2021. 4.4: 35% Annual Resource Delivery.
It is important to note that Project invalidation in September 2020, by the Government made it difficult to implement some of the planned activities like institutional strengthening, including much of the critical work especially with the Electoral Commission.

Output 1: Strengthened inclusion and transparency of the electoral process. Results attained under output 1: 1) Stakeholder engagement, dialogues and mobilization of women voters was undertaken through regional Stakeholder workshops with Electoral Commission and CSOs, FBOs, Media, Political Parties, observers, SIGs, MDAs LGs, Political party women leagues, development partners, state and non-state actors. 2) Electoral Commission focused on supporting the preparation, development, popularization and display of the voter register for the Women Council elections. 3) Electoral Commission also raised awareness about registration for the Women Council elections via media outlets such as radio and press statements.
Output 2: Enhanced institutional capacity for the Electoral Commission and other electoral stakeholders Results attained under output 2: 1) Initiated key activities with the Judiciary including: i) Installation and set-up of Video conferencing installation for Mubende High Court and Kaweeri Prison; ii) Development of training and learning tools on electoral dispute resolution; iii) Development of a Curriculum for training Court transcribers; iv) Training of Judicial Officers; v) South to South exchange and learning visit to Ghana; vi) Documentation and knowledge management; 2) OHCHR supported UHRC to conduct a high-level training for UPDF command officers on human rights standards in the context of UPDF operations to provide security during the Women Councils and committees elections 2022; 3) OHCHR supported UHRC to conduct a high-level training for CMI operational officers on human rights standards in the context of security operations to provide security during the Women Councils and committees elections 2022; and 4) Training of UPF on maintaining law and order and Production of Civic/Voter Education materials, including spot messages. 5) Women International Peace Centre conducted an end of project evaluation for the Women Situation Room (WSR) to establish the extent to which the project has achieved its objectives: Key findings include -The WSR project interventions are still relevant since the benefits are enormous. These include capacity building of women and youth, reduction of violence and peace building, support towards household incomes enhancement, among others. -The project managed to achieve its objectives towards providing women and youth with a platform to make a contribution towards curbing election violence and promoting peace among their communities. -The project interventions were delivered in time and thus it managed to achieve the objectives, while resources were also optimally deployed. -Project initiatives generally led to promotion of peace within the intervention communities. -Through focusing on building capacity of women and youth, project initiatives are easily sustained especially towards eradication of violence and peace building. -Project intervention made a great contribution towards the achievement of objectives of the NDP III programs. -The report is still in draft and will be reviewed by the Eminent Women who will provide feedback for the consultant to finalize. 6) UNDP in partnership with the UN family and Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC) provided support to the dialogue in commemoration of the International Day of Peace.
Output 3: Effective and Efficient Management, Partnership Formation, Research, Monitoring and Evaluation of the Women Councils/Committees Elections Results attained under output 3: Engagement across project stakeholders and developments 1) Strategic engagements were held to inform the direction of the SEPU project. Key among these included with 2) Government leadership (Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Prime Minister and Electoral Commission), Donor and UN Agencies meetings and the EC Strategic plan meeting. Consequently, further technical level engagements have been undertaken with the Electoral Commission and other relevant stakeholders where the workplan was finalized and implementation of the work plan was activated. 3) Key analysis was undertaken by two consultants including a political economy analysis in Uganda by Dr Frederick Golooba and an analysis of the Governance, peace and development emerging issues in Uganda by Prof. Christopher Mbazira.

This indicator assess the level of trust and faith that the general public has in the Body responsible for overseeing and conducting elections within a country/Election Commission (EC). This indicator is essential for evaluating the credibility and legitimacy of the electoral process. It takes into consideration the aspect of citizens’ perceptions of election quality and how well they think the national election management body does its job of ensuring transparent and competent elections.

description.narrative: This indicator quantifies gender balance among candidates running for political office in elections conducted at both the national and sub-national (regional or local) levels. It assess the level of gender diversity and women's representation in the political process. The formula to calculate this indicator is as follows: Percentage of Women Candidates (to Men Candidates)=(Number of Women Candidates/Total number Candidates)×100% In this formula: • Number of Women Candidates: This represents the count of women who have declared their candidacy to run for political office in a specific election, whether it's at the national or sub-national level. • Total number of Candidates: This refers to the count of all candidates who have declared their candidacy for the same election or political positions.

title.narrative: Proportion of eligible voters who are registered to vote, disaggregated by sex, age, and excluded groups

description.narrative: "This indicator quantifies the percentage of individuals who are eligible to vote and have successfully registered to vote in a particular election or within a defined timeframe. This indicator provides insight into the level of voter participation. The formula to calculate this indicator is as follows: Proportion of Eligible Voters Registered to Vote= (Number of Registered Voters/ Number of Eligible Voters) ×100% In this formula: • Number of Registered Voters: This represents the count of individuals who have completed the voter registration process and are thus eligible to participate in elections. • Number of Eligible Voters: This refers to the total number of individuals who meet the eligibility criteria for voting in a specific election or jurisdiction. Eligibility criteria typically include factors such as citizenship, age, and residency.
